    Government of India, NIFT collaborates with ministries, public institutions, industry bodies and state governments.

    These partnerships drive policy initiatives, craft development programmes, research collaborations and national projects that strengthen India's design ecosystem.

    Each centre brings its own regional strengths, industry connections, craft traditions and academic expertise, while remaining part of a single institution committed to excellence in design education.

    Crafting Stories in Clay- The Legacy of Krishnanagar's Artisans

    Understanding a country's art, craft, culture, and traditions plays a vital role in shaping identity and inspiring creative thinking. To explore the renowned clay doll craft of Krishnanagar, the Fashion & Lifestyle Accessory Department of NIFT Kolkata conducted a 10-day field study in West Bengal. Through interactions with skilled artisans, detailed documentation, and firsthand cultural experiences, the research team gained valuable insights into the craftsmanship, heritage, and challenges faced by the artisan community. This study presents a comprehensive overview of the craft and its makers.
    --

    Designing Futures. Transforming Lives.

    For four decades NIFT has shaped India's fashion ecosystem through education, research, innovation and industry collaboration.

    From classrooms and studios to craft clusters and global collaborations, NIFT prepares students to lead with creativity, purpose and impact.

    New Delhi Campus

    Established in Delhi in 1986, NIFT initially offered a single Fashion Design programme, operating from a provisional two-room facility before relocating to a permanent campus in 1994. Conceived by Dr. B.V. Doshi, the building draws upon the Indian baoli, employing a central step-well for rainwater conservation, and is recognised among Delhi's iconic modern architecture. Initially comprising four programmes, two postgraduate and two undergraduate.The institute is now NIFT's largest campus, offering all seven bachelor's and three master's programmes with the largest enrolment

    The National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) Delhi successfully hosted a vibrant Handloom Day celebration on August 7, 2026. As detailed in the event posters, the celebration honoured traditional weavers while looking toward the future of sustainable fashion. Coordinated by CIC Dr. Tulika Mahanty, the event featured a curated two-day Mini Craft Bazaar (August 6th & 7th) on the 3rd floor, alongside a captivating exhibition on the 2nd floor that showcased the creative works of textile design students. A major highlight was the panel discussion in the 4th-floor auditorium themed, "Handloom for Gen Z: Reimagining Slow Fashion." Led by esteemed panellists Mr. Parvez Alam (Project Director ,Antaran, Tata Trusts) and designer Aman Hussain, the session engaged Semester 1 students in critical conversations about design innovation, sustainable consumption, and artisan empowerment. The celebration successfully bridged the gap between traditional craftsmanship and the next generation of designers.

    --

    NIFT New Delhi commemorated the 80th Independence Day with a ceremonial observance attended by faculty, staff, and students. The National Flag was unfurled by Director Prof. Shinju Mahajan, followed by a cultural programme reflecting the collective spirit of the occasion. The Literary Club presented patriotic recitations, complemented by dance performances set to nationalist compositions and a musical rendition by Rang. The gathering underscored the campus community's shared commitment to the values enshrined in the nation's independence.
